services.label: expertise
services.title: what I do
services.intro: Six areas I work in every day. Each one lists what I have hands-on experience with.

cards.title: Network & firewall
cards.desc: I design VLAN schemes, segment networks and manage routing, firewall policy and VPN. I have worked with Fortinet (FortiGate), Ubiquiti (UniFi, EFG), Cisco, WatchGuard, Dell, Barracuda, Netgear, Zyxel and pfSense.

cards.title: Systems & virtualisation
cards.desc: Windows Server with Active Directory and GPO, Linux servers, and virtualisation on Nutanix (AHV, Prism), VMware vSphere (vCenter, ESXi) and Hyper-V. Work that keeps coming back gets scripted in PowerShell, Python or Bash.

cards.title: Microsoft 365 & identity
cards.desc: Administration of Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, Entra ID with Hybrid join, and devices through Intune. Also experience with certificates from a private PKI with SCEP.

cards.title: Backup & recovery
cards.desc: With Veeam I have done a lot of backups and restores on Nutanix, VMware vSphere and Hyper-V. I also work with a cloud backup platform. I test restores and document what came back and what did not.

cards.title: Monitoring
cards.desc: Zabbix with agents and SNMP, dashboards and alerting, plus Windows Event Log.

cards.title: Security
cards.desc: Hardening, segmentation and firewall policy, EDR on servers, and network access with 802.1X and certificates. For detection and secure remote access I have worked with Wazuh, NetBird and OpenZiti.

about.label: about
paragraphs: I'm Ali Tunç, a system and network administrator. I work full-time for an international manufacturer. I manage, maintain and improve the infrastructure there and take part in IT projects. IT at one of the sites is my responsibility. Now and then we do configuration and maintenance on location at sites abroad.

Recent work: moved laptops to a new domain with Hybrid Entra ID join, rolled out an EDR agent to the servers, ran and documented restore tests, fitted ISP routers and a core switch in behind the firewall, and analysed connection problems with cloud telephony for more than a hundred users on the firewall side.
I have a few fixed habits. I write down what I do, in runbooks a colleague can follow. I test before I roll anything out. And a backup only counts once the restore has worked.
Security is part of the daily work: hardening, segmentation, firewall policy, EDR. In an isolated lab I test attacks and defences. What I see there goes back into how I run things.

cards.title: Laptops to a new domain
cards.problem: Laptops were still joined to the old domain and had to move to the new one.
cards.approach: Moved them one by one with Hybrid Entra ID join. The steps are in a runbook I wrote myself.

cards.title: EDR on the servers
cards.problem: The servers were still running an older antivirus product.
cards.approach: Rolled out an EDR agent to the servers to replace it.

cards.title: Backup and restore tests
cards.problem: Checking that backups can actually be restored.
cards.approach: Ran restore tests on Veeam and on a cloud backup platform.
cards.result: Every test and its outcome is documented.

cards.title: ISP routers and core switch behind the firewall
cards.problem: New ISP routers and a core switch had to be fitted into the existing network.
cards.approach: Drew up the IP plan and integrated the devices behind the firewall.

cards.title: Connection problems with cloud telephony
cards.problem: Cloud telephony for more than 100 users had connection problems.
cards.approach: Analysed the traffic on the firewall side to find the cause.

cards.title: Emergency phones for fire prevention
cards.problem: A fire prevention project needed managed emergency phones.
cards.approach: Enrolled and managed the devices through MDM.

cards.title: Handheld scanners to a new server
cards.problem: Handheld barcode scanners had to move to a new server.
cards.approach: Prepared the switch and tested the scanners against the new server.

cards.title: Network renewal for a local government
cards.problem: A local government's network was due for a redesign.
cards.approach: Documented as-is and to-be, designed a VLAN scheme on the Core-Distribution-Access model, and compared switches, firewalls and access points on performance, availability and budget.
cards.result: The documentation is the basis for the implementation and for NIS2 compliance.

cards.title: Zabbix monitoring and Wazuh SIEM
cards.problem: Getting a central view of servers, network devices and security events.
cards.approach: Set up Zabbix with SNMP and agents, dashboards, alerting and Windows Event Log. Alongside it Wazuh as XDR/SIEM, with Windows agents, active response and rule-based alerting.

cards.title: Remote access with NetBird (ZTNA)
cards.problem: Secure access from outside to the internal infrastructure.
cards.approach: Installed and configured a self-hosted NetBird as Zero Trust Network Access.

cards.title: PacketFence NAC with EAP-TLS
cards.problem: Certificate-based Wi-Fi access for an environment of 106 schools.
cards.approach: Designed and built in a lab environment: PacketFence NAC with 802.1X and EAP-TLS, a private PKI and Intune for the certificates. Certificate rollout automated with PowerShell.

cards.title: Zero trust with OpenZiti and Entra ID
cards.problem: Access to services based on identity and certificates.
cards.approach: Set up a zero-trust architecture with OpenZiti in a lab environment, tied to Microsoft Entra ID.
